kubernetes.description: The kubernetes manager ships NO default file matching, because a .yaml file could be anything. Without these patterns Renovate never reads a single `image:` line in this repo, which is how bookorbit sat on 3.5.0 while four upstream releases shipped and Renovate kept bumping go.mod.

kustomize.description: A separate manager on purpose: an image pinned through a kustomization.yaml `images:` transformer is invisible to the kubernetes manager above.

packageRules.description: Group ALL non-major updates into a single weekly PR (no more one-PR-per-package spam)
Group all GitHub Actions bumps into one PR

All non-major container image bumps land in ONE PR, and NEVER automerge. Flux reconciles main, so merging an image bump here deploys it: there is no staging step between the merge button and production. Fine for a go.mod bump, not fine for a container serving traffic, so a human presses the button. Scoped to non-major so majors fall through to the rule below and stay on their own.

Isolate major updates so each gets its own review. groupName null keeps a major OUT of the grouped PRs above, which it would otherwise inherit, because Renovate merges every matching rule rather than applying only the last one.

Apps that run irreversible schema migrations on boot. Nothing above automerges images any more, so this no longer exists to block that; it exists to LABEL the PR, so whoever reviews the grouped image PR can see it contains something that will migrate a live database on the next pod start. BookOrbit applies forward migrations as the new pod boots: the image rolls back, the schema does not, and a 3.5.0 binary against a 3.9.0 schema will not start. Take a backup first, the way bookorbit-pre-3-5-0 and bookorbit-pre-latest-upgrade were. Deliberately does NOT set groupName, so these stay inside the single grouped PR instead of fragmenting it.
